problem_text:
A transportation provider plans a set of profitable vehicle operations while simultaneously building a feasible crew plan that can cover those operations. Both the vehicle side and the crew side are represented as discrete time-space transitions: selecting a transition means committing to a specific movement or linkage in the plan.

During the planning horizon, there are 21 independent starting requirements. For each requirement, exactly one starting option must be chosen so that a corresponding operational stream can begin.

Some operational blocks are only meaningful if they are opened and properly “anchored” at both ends. The instance contains 320 such blocks. When a block is opened, exactly two associated boundary choices must be selected, reflecting that the block must have a valid start and a valid end within the overall plan.

Operational activity is also paced across 20 windows. In each window, the number of selected vehicle-side transitions must remain within a window-specific band and must not exceed a hard limit. In addition, there are 8 policy dimensions that limit how concentrated certain vehicle-side attributes can be among the selected transitions.

The plan must also satisfy minimum coverage expectations across 52 groups and avoid incompatible combinations captured by 88 conflict groups. Finally, some choices only make sense when at least one supporting continuation is also chosen.

Each selectable choice has a net cost that can be positive (expense) or negative (profit credit). The goal is to select a consistent set of choices that respects all operational rules and yields the minimum total net cost.
